Fit a model to mortality data

Source: R/model-spec.R
mt_fit.Rd

Applies the preprocessing pipeline, takes deaths and exposures on the grid and fits the model per stratum (or jointly). A failure in one stratum is recorded in the diagnostics and does not stop the other strata.

Usage

mt_fit(spec, data, prep = NULL, cores = 1, ...)

Arguments

spec

A model specification (mt_spec).

data

An mt_data object.

prep

An mt_prep pipeline or NULL.

cores

Number of cores for per-stratum fits (forked processes; 1 on Windows). Each stratum is fitted with its own random number stream, started from the seed of the specification (seed of lee_carter()) or else from the current generator, so fits that use random numbers (such as lee_carter(bootstrap = TRUE)) are reproduced by that seed or by set.seed() with any number of cores.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

An object of class mt_fit.

Details

Smooth inside the fit (prep = mt_prep(step_smooth(...))), not before it: data returned by mt_smooth() carry no raw deaths, so residuals and observation noise would refer to the smoothed rates and the intervals would be too narrow. Such data give a warning.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
fit <- mt_fit(lee_carter(), x)
fit
#> <mt_fit> Lee-Carter; 2 strata; ages 30 to 100+; periods 1990-2019
